title: 'Flock Flocked up'

reading.body:
This is a case of a system acting on a false match and a use-of-force decision that followed from it. An automated licence plate reader flagged a vehicle as stolen when the plate it read belonged to a different car, and officers treated that flag as grounds for a stop. The failure sits at the point where a machine-generated alert enters a human decision chain without independent verification of the underlying record.

The escalation that followed, the K-9 deployment, the arrest and the charges, is a separate decision made by officers on the scene. The department's own policy required handlers to weigh the severity of the crime, any immediate threat, and whether a suspect was resisting or fleeing. Catching the error would have required confirming the plate against the actual vehicle or the source record before acting on the alert, rather than after.

What is not established from these reports is whether the camera's misread was a known limitation, how often such misreads occur, or what the outcome of the investigation into the officers will be. The department's review found no wrongdoing in the K-9 use, and the charges were later dropped, but neither of those is a finding about the accuracy of the camera system itself.

reports.title: Body cam of TPD officers releasing K-9 on man during traffic stop
Man speaks out after police release K-9 on him during traffic stop: 'Traumatized'
TPD investigation finds no wrongdoing in use of K-9 on man during traffic stop
Charges dropped against man Toledo Police released K-9 on during traffic stop, lawyer says

summary:
Toledo Police released body camera video showing officers using a K-9 on a driver during a traffic stop. An officer stopped a red Dodge Ram after a FLOCK camera incorrectly flagged its plate as stolen, because the camera misread a plate belonging to a Chevy Malibu. The driver, Brandon Upchurch, got out with his hands up, and officers ordered him to the ground. He was arrested and charged with resisting arrest and obstruction. He received medical attention at the scene.

Officers later learned the plate information was wrong. Police said they believed the driver might flee and did not know if he or a passenger had weapons. The department's K-9 policy says handlers should weigh the crime's severity, any immediate threat, and whether a suspect is resisting or fleeing. Multiple officers are under investigation, and the body camera footage was released Monday.
